sentences.zh: 列傳第六十八 列女 ○阿鄰妻 李寶信妻 韓慶民妻 雷婦師氏 康住住 李文妻 李英妻 相琪妻 阿魯真 撒合輦妻 許古妻 馮妙真 蒲察氏 烏古論氏 素蘭妻 忙哥妻 尹氏 白氏 聶孝女 仲德妻 寶符李氏 張鳳奴

translations.literal: Biography 68 Exemplary Women: Wife of A Lin, Wife of Li Baoxin, Wife of Han Qingmin, Lady Shi of Leifu, Kang Zhuzhu, Wife of Li Wen, Wife of Li Ying, Wife of Xiang Qi, A Luzhen, Wife of Sahe Nian, Wife of Xu Gu, Feng Miaozhen, Lady Pucha, Lady Wugulun, Wife of Su Lan, Wife of Mang Ge, Lady Yin, Lady Bai, Nie Xiaonu, Wife of Zhong De, Lady Li of Baofu, Zhang Fengnu
translations.idiomatic: Biography 68 — Exemplary Women: the wife of A Lin; the wife of Li Baoxin; the wife of Han Qingmin; Lady Shi of Leifu; Kang Zhuzhu; the wife of Li Wen; the wife of Li Ying; the wife of Xiang Qi; A Luzhen; the wife of Sahe Nian; the wife of Xu Gu; Feng Miaozhen; Lady Pucha; Lady Wugulun; the wife of Su Lan; the wife of Mang Ge; Lady Yin; Lady Bai; Nie Xiaonu; the wife of Zhong De; Lady Li of Baofu; Zhang Fengnu

sentences.zh: 漢成帝時，劉向始述三代賢妃淑女，及淫泆奢僭、興亡盛衰之所由，匯分類別，號《列女傳》，因以諷諫。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Cheng of Han, Liu Xiang first narrated the worthy consorts and virtuous ladies of the Three Dynasties, and the causes of licentiousness, extravagance, overstepping of bounds, and the rise and fall, flourishing and decline [of states]; he gathered and classified them, titled it Biographies of Exemplary Women, and thereby offered admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng of Han, Liu Xiang first set down the worthy consorts and virtuous ladies of the Three Dynasties, together with accounts of debauchery, extravagance, presumption, and the causes of dynastic rise and fall; he sorted these into categories under the title Biographies of Exemplary Women, using them as moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 范曄始載之漢史。

translations.literal: Fan Ye first recorded them in the History of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye was the first to include such figures in the History of Han.

sentences.zh: 古者女子生十年有女師，漸長，有麻枲絲繭之事，有祭祀助奠之事；

translations.literal: In antiquity, when a girl reached ten years of age she had a female instructor; as she gradually grew, there were matters of hemp, ramie, silk, and cocoon-reeling, and matters of assisting at sacrifices and libations;
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times a girl of ten was given a female tutor; as she grew she was taught hemp and ramie work, silk and sericulture, and how to assist at sacrifices and offerings;

sentences.zh: 既嫁，職在中饋而已，故以無非無儀為賢。

translations.literal: Once married, her duty lay only in the inner household, and therefore to be without fault and without impropriety was deemed virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: After marriage her sphere was the inner household alone, and virtue meant simply never giving cause for blame or scandal.

sentences.zh: 若乃嫠居寡處，患難顛沛，是皆婦人之不幸也。

translations.literal: As for living as a widow in solitude, or suffering hardship and destitution — these are all a woman's misfortunes.
translations.idiomatic: Widowhood, isolation, hardship, and ruin are among the greatest misfortunes that can befall a woman.

sentences.zh: 一遇不幸，卓然能自樹立，有烈丈夫之風，是以君子異之。

translations.literal: When once they meet misfortune yet can stand forth outstandingly on their own, with the spirit of a stern great man — for this the gentleman marks them as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when misfortune strikes and a woman can still hold herself upright with the mettle of a resolute man, the cultivated reader takes special note of her.

sentences.zh: 阿鄰妻

translations.literal: Wife of A Lin
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of A Lin

sentences.zh: 阿鄰妻沙裏質者，金源郡王銀術可之妹。

translations.literal: The wife of A Lin, Shalizhi, was the younger sister of Prince of Jinyuan Commandery Yinsuke.
translations.idiomatic: A Lin's wife Shalizhi was a younger sister of Yinsuke, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，黃龍府叛卒攻鈔旁近部族。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, rebel soldiers of Huanglong Prefecture attacked and plundered nearby tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu (1122), mutineers from Huanglong Prefecture raided neighboring tribal settlements.

sentences.zh: 是時，阿鄰從軍，沙裏質糾集附近居民得男女五百人，樹營柵為保守計。

translations.literal: At that time A Lin was on campaign; Shalizhi gathered nearby inhabitants, obtaining five hundred men and women, and erected palisades as a plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: A Lin was away on campaign; Shalizhi rallied local residents until she had five hundred men and women, then threw up stockades to hold the position.

sentences.zh: 賊千余來攻，沙裏質以氈為甲，以裳為旗，男夫授甲，婦女鼓噪，沙裏質仗劍督戰，凡三日賊去。

translations.literal: More than a thousand bandits came to attack; Shalizhi used felt for armor and skirts for banners; the men were given armor, the women raised a clamor; Shalizhi wielded a sword to supervise the battle — after three days the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a thousand rebels attacked, she improvised armor from felt and standards from skirts, armed the men, set the women to shouting, and herself took sword in hand to direct the fight; after three days the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，論功封金源郡夫人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong, her merit was discussed and she was enfeoffed as Lady of Jinyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangtong (1142) her service was rewarded with the title Lady of Jinyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 大定間，以其孫藥師為謀克。

translations.literal: During the Dading era, her grandson Yaoshi was made a military commander (mouke).
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong (Dading reign), her grandson Yaoshi was appointed a company commander (mouke).

sentences.zh: 李寶信妻

translations.literal: Wife of Li Baoxin
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Li Baoxin

sentences.zh: 李寶信妻王氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Baoxin was the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoxin's wife was a woman of the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 寶信為義豐縣令，張覺以平州叛，王氏陷賊中。

translations.literal: Baoxin was magistrate of Yifeng County; Zhang Jue rebelled with Pingzhou, and Lady Wang fell into the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxin served as magistrate of Yifeng County; when Zhang Jue rose in rebellion at Pingzhou, Lady Wang was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊欲逼室之，王氏罵賊，賊怒遂支解之。

translations.literal: The rebels wished to force her into the inner quarters; Lady Wang cursed the rebels, and in their rage they dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to take her into their quarters; she cursed them, and in fury they hacked her to pieces.

sentences.zh: 大定十二年，贈「貞烈縣君」。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dading, she was posthumously granted the title "Chaste and Steadfast County Lady."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Dading (1172) she was posthumously ennobled as Chaste and Steadfast County Lady.

sentences.zh: 韓慶民妻

translations.literal: Wife of Han Qingmin
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Han Qingmin

sentences.zh: 韓慶民妻者，不知何許人，亦不知其姓氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Han Qingmin — it is not known of what place she was, nor is her surname known.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qingmin's wife — neither her native place nor her family name is recorded.

sentences.zh: 慶民事遼為宜州節度使。

translations.literal: Qingmin served the Liao as military commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qingmin had served the Liao dynasty as military commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 天會中，攻破宜州，慶民不屈而死，以其妻配將士，其妻誓死不從，遂自殺。

translations.literal: During the Tianhui era, [the Jin] captured Yizhou; Qingmin died without yielding, and his wife was given in marriage to officers and soldiers; his wife vowed she would rather die than submit, and thereupon killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui period the Jin took Yizhou; Qingmin refused to submit and was put to death, and his wife was allotted to the troops; she swore she would never yield and took her own life.

sentences.zh: 世宗讀《太宗實錄》，見慶民夫婦事，歎曰：「如此節操，可謂難矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, reading the Veritable Records of Taizong, saw the affair of Qingmin and his wife and sighed, saying: "Such integrity of conduct — one may call it rare."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong read the Veritable Records of Taizong and came upon the story of Qingmin and his wife, he sighed and said, "Devotion of that order is truly hard to find."

sentences.zh: 雷婦師氏

translations.literal: Lady Shi of Leifu
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi of Leifu

sentences.zh: 雷婦師氏，夫亡，孝養舅姑。

translations.literal: Lady Shi of Leifu — her husband died; she filially nurtured her parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi of Leifu lost her husband and devoted herself to caring for her parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑病，刲臂肉飼之，姑即愈。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law fell ill; she cut flesh from her arm to feed her, and her mother-in-law promptly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill, she cut flesh from her own arm to feed her, and the elder woman soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 舅姑既歿。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law had both passed away,
translations.idiomatic: After both parents-in-law had died,

sentences.zh: 兄師逵與夫侄規其財產，乃偽立謀證致之官，欲必嫁之。

translations.literal: her elder brother Shi Kui and her husband's nephew plotted over her property; they falsely set up evidence and brought the case to the authorities, wishing to force her to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: her elder brother Shi Kui and her husband's nephew schemed for her estate; they fabricated evidence and hauled her before the magistrate, intent on forcing her to remarry.

sentences.zh: 縣官不能辨曲直，師氏畏逼，乃投縣署井中死。

translations.literal: The county magistrate could not distinguish right from wrong; Lady Shi, fearing coercion, threw herself into the county-office well and died.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate could not settle the dispute; cornered by pressure, Lady Shi threw herself into the county well and drowned.

sentences.zh: 詔有司祭其墓，賜諡曰「節」。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to sacrifice at her tomb and granted the posthumous title "Chaste."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered official sacrifices at her tomb and granted her the posthumous epithet Chaste.

sentences.zh: 康住住

translations.literal: Kang Zhuzhu
translations.idiomatic: Kang Zhuzhu

sentences.zh: 康住住，鄜州人。

translations.literal: Kang Zhuzhu was a native of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Zhuzhu came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 夫早亡，服闋，父取之歸家，許嚴沂為妻。

translations.literal: Her husband died early; when the mourning period ended, her father took her back home and betrothed her to Yan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband died young; when her mourning ended her father brought her home and promised her to Yan Yi.

sentences.zh: 康氏誓死弗聽，欲還夫家不可得，乃投崖而死。

translations.literal: Lady Kang vowed she would rather die than obey; wishing to return to her husband's house yet unable to do so, she cast herself from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Kang swore she would die before obeying; unable to return to her husband's household, she leapt from a cliff to her death.

sentences.zh: 詔有司致祭其墓。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to perform sacrifices at her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered official rites at her grave.

sentences.zh: 李文妻

translations.literal: Wife of Li Wen
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Li Wen

sentences.zh: 李文妻史氏，同州白水人。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Wen, of the Shi clan, was a native of Baishui in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wen's wife, née Shi, was from Baishui in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 夫亡，服闋，誓死弗嫁。

translations.literal: Her husband died; when the mourning period ended, she vowed she would rather die than remarry.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband's death and the end of mourning, she swore never to marry again.

sentences.zh: 父強取之歸，許邑人姚乙為妻。

translations.literal: Her father forcibly took her back and betrothed her to Yao Yi, a man of the district.
translations.idiomatic: Her father seized her back and betrothed her to a local man named Yao Yi.

sentences.zh: 史氏不聽，姚訴之官，被逮，遂自縊死。

translations.literal: Lady Shi would not obey; Yao brought suit at court; she was seized, and thereupon hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi refused; Yao sued before the magistrate; when she was taken into custody she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 詔有司致祭其墓。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to perform sacrifices at her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered sacrifices at her tomb.

sentences.zh: 李英妻

translations.literal: Wife of Li Ying
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Li Ying

sentences.zh: 李英妻張氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Ying was the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying's wife was a woman of the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 英初為監察禦史，在中都，張居濰州。

translations.literal: Ying was at first a supervising censor at the Central Capital; Zhang resided at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had first served as supervising censor at the Central Capital while Lady Zhang remained at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年冬，大元兵取濰州，入其家，張氏盡以所有財物與之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Zhenyou, the Great Yuan army took Weizhou and entered their house; Lady Zhang gave them all her possessions.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Zhenyou (1213) the Mongol army captured Weizhou and entered their home; Lady Zhang surrendered everything she owned.

sentences.zh: 既而，令張氏上馬，張曰：「我盡以物與汝，猶不見贖邪？

translations.literal: Presently they ordered Lady Zhang to mount a horse; Zhang said: "I have given you all my goods — do you still not see fit to ransom me?
translations.idiomatic: Then they told her to mount a horse; she said, "I have given you everything I own — will you still not let me go?

sentences.zh: 」答曰「汝品官妻，當複為夫人。

translations.literal: " They answered: "You are the wife of a ranked official — you shall again become a lady.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "You are a ranking official's wife — you will be a lady again.

sentences.zh: 」張曰：「我死則為李氏鬼。

translations.literal: " Zhang said: "If I die, I shall be a ghost of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "If I die, I die a ghost of the Li household.

sentences.zh: 頓坐不起，遂見殺。

translations.literal: She sat down abruptly and would not rise, and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: She dropped to the ground and would not rise, and they killed her.

sentences.zh: 追封隴西郡夫人，諡「莊潔」。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi Commandery, with the posthumous title "Solemn and Pure."
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously created Lady of Longxi Commandery with the epithet Solemn and Pure.

sentences.zh: 英仕至御史中丞，有傳。

translations.literal: Ying rose in office to Vice Censor-in-Chief; he has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ying rose to vice censor-in-chief and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 相琪妻

translations.literal: Wife of Xiang Qi
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Xiang Qi

sentences.zh: 相琪妻欒氏，有姿色。

translations.literal: The wife of Xiang Qi, of the Luan clan, had beauty of form.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Qi's wife, née Luan, was a woman of striking beauty.

sentences.zh: 琪為萊州掖縣司吏。

translations.literal: Qi was a clerk of Ye County in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi served as a clerk in Ye County, Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年八月，紅祆賊陷掖縣，琪與欒氏及子俱為所得。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyou, the Red Turban bandits captured Ye County; Qi, Lady Luan, and their son were all taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyou (1215) Red Turban rebels overran Ye County; Qi, Lady Luan, and their son were all captured.

sentences.zh: 賊見欒悅之，殺琪及其子而誘欒。

translations.literal: The bandits, pleased upon seeing Luan, killed Qi and his son and tried to entice Luan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took a fancy to Luan, murdered Qi and their son, and tried to seduce her.

sentences.zh: 欒奮起以頭觸賊而僕，罵曰：「我豈為犬彘所汙者哉。

translations.literal: Luan sprang up and struck the bandit with her head, knocking him down, and cursed: "How could I be defiled by dogs and swine!
translations.idiomatic: Luan sprang up, butted the rebel to the ground, and cried, "Would I let myself be fouled by dogs and swine!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，殺之。

translations.literal: " The bandits in anger killed her.
translations.idiomatic: " Enraged, they slew her.

sentences.zh: 追封西河縣君，諡「莊潔」。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as County Lady of Xihe, with the posthumous title "Solemn and Pure."
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously created County Lady of Xihe with the epithet Solemn and Pure.

sentences.zh: 阿魯真

translations.literal: A Luzhen
translations.idiomatic: A Luzhen

sentences.zh: 撒合輦妻

translations.literal: Wife of Sahe Nian
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Sahe Nian

sentences.zh: 獨吉氏，平章政事千家奴之女，護衛銀術可妹也。

translations.literal: Of the Dugu clan — daughter of the Grand Councilor Qianjianu, and younger sister of the guardsman Yinsuke.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dugu was a daughter of Grand Councilor Qianjianu and younger sister of the guardsman Yinsuke.

sentences.zh: 自幼動有禮法，及適內族撒合輦。

translations.literal: From childhood her movements observed ritual propriety; when she married into the inner clan, Sahe Nian,
translations.idiomatic: From girlhood her conduct was governed by ritual; she was given in marriage within the imperial clan to Sahe Nian.

sentences.zh: 閨門肅如。

translations.literal: the inner quarters were as solemn as if in a hall of ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Her household was run with the gravity of a court audience hall.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦為中京留守，大兵圍之，撒合輦疽發背不能軍，獨吉氏度城必破，謂撒合輦曰：「公本無功能，徒以宗室故嘗在禁近，以至提點近侍局，同判睦親府，今又為留守外路第一等官，受國家恩最厚。

translations.literal: Sahe Nian was military governor of the Central Capital; the great army besieged it; Sahe Nian had a carbuncle on his back and could not command the troops; Lady Dugu judged the city would surely fall, and said to Sahe Nian: "Your Lordship originally had no ability — you were only by reason of the imperial clan once near the forbidden precincts, until you reached superintendent of the Inner Service Bureau and associate director of the Bureau of Imperial Kin, and now again are military governor, the foremost official on an outer circuit, receiving the state's favor most thickly.
translations.idiomatic: Sahe Nian was military governor of the Central Capital when a great army laid siege to the city; a carbuncle on his back left him unable to take the field. Lady Dugu saw that the city must fall and told him, "You never had real talent — you rose only because you are of the imperial clan, first near the inner palace, then superintendent of the Inner Service Bureau and associate director of the Bureau of Imperial Kin, and now military governor, the highest post on an outer circuit, enjoying the deepest favor of the state.

sentences.zh: 今大兵臨城，公不幸病，不能戰禦，設若城破，公當率精銳奪門而出，攜一子走京師。

translations.literal: Now the great army is before the walls; Your Lordship is unfortunately ill and cannot fight in defense; if the city should fall, Your Lordship ought to lead picked troops to seize the gate and break out, taking one son and fleeing to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy is at the walls and you are too ill to defend them. If the city falls, lead your best troops through the gate, take one son, and flee to the capital.

sentences.zh: 不能則獨赴京師，又不能，戰而死猶可報國，幸無以我為慮。

translations.literal: If you cannot, then go alone to the capital; if you cannot even that, to die fighting can still repay the state — only do not worry on my account.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot manage that, go to the capital alone; if you cannot do even that, die fighting and you will still have repaid the dynasty — but do not trouble yourself over me.

sentences.zh: 」撒合輦出巡城，獨吉氏乃取平日衣服妝具玩好布之臥榻，資貨悉散之家人，豔妝盛服過於平日，且戒女使曰：「我死則扶置榻上，以衾覆面，四圍舉火焚之。

translations.literal: " Sahe Nian went out to inspect the walls; Lady Dugu then took her usual garments, toilet implements, and cherished objects and spread them on the couch-bed, distributed all valuables among the household, dressed more splendidly than on ordinary days, and moreover charged the serving women: "When I die, support my body on the couch-bed, cover my face with a quilt, and set fires all around to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: " Sahe Nian went out to inspect the defenses. Lady Dugu laid out her everyday clothes, cosmetics, and favorite things on the bed, gave away all the household valuables, dressed more richly than on any ordinary day, and instructed her maids: "When I am dead, lay me on the bed, cover my face with a quilt, and burn everything around me.

sentences.zh: 無使兵見吾面。

translations.literal: Do not let the soldiers see my face.
translations.idiomatic: Let no soldier see my face.

sentences.zh: 」言訖，閉門自經而死。

translations.literal: " When she had finished speaking, she shut the door and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " With that she shut the door and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 家人如言，臥屍榻上，以衾覆之。

translations.literal: The household did as she had said, laying the corpse on the couch-bed and covering it with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: The household obeyed: they laid her body on the bed and covered it.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦從外室，家人告以夫人之死，撒合輦拊榻曰：「夫人不辱我，我肯辱朝廷乎！

translations.literal: Sahe Nian came from the outer chamber; the household told him of his lady's death; Sahe Nian struck the couch and said: "My lady did not disgrace me — would I disgrace the court!
translations.idiomatic: Sahe Nian returned from outside; when they told him his wife was dead he beat the bed and cried, "My wife did not shame me — shall I shame the throne!

sentences.zh: 」因命焚之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered it burned.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the pyre lit.

sentences.zh: 年三十有六。

translations.literal: Her age was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 少頃，城破，撒合輦率死士欲奪門出，不果，投壕水死，有傳。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter the city fell; Sahe Nian led death-defying soldiers wishing to seize the gate and break out — it did not succeed; he cast himself into the moat-water and died; he has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell; Sahe Nian led a band of men willing to die trying to break out through the gate, failed, and drowned himself in the moat; he too has a biography.

sentences.zh: 許古妻

translations.literal: Wife of Xu Gu
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Xu Gu

sentences.zh: 許古妻劉氏，定海軍節度使仲洙之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Xu Gu, of the Liu clan, was the daughter of Liu Zhongzhu, military commissioner of Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gu's wife, née Liu, was a daughter of Liu Zhongzhu, military commissioner of the Dinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，古挈家僑居蒲城，從留劉氏母子于蒲，仕於朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, Gu took his household to sojourn at Pucheng, leaving Lady Liu and her sons at Pu while he took office at court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyou era Gu moved his family to Pucheng, leaving Lady Liu and their children there while he took office at court.

sentences.zh: 既而，兵圍蒲，劉謂二女曰：「汝父在朝，而兵勢如此，事不可保。

translations.literal: Presently troops besieged Pu; Liu said to her two daughters: "Your father is at court, yet the military situation is thus — the affair cannot be assured.
translations.idiomatic: When troops soon besieged Pucheng, Lady Liu told her two daughters, "Your father is at court and the armies press so hard that nothing is secure.

sentences.zh: 若城破被驅，一為所汙奈何？

translations.literal: If the city falls and we are driven off, what if we are defiled — how then?
translations.idiomatic: If the city falls and we are dragged away, how could we bear to be violated?

sentences.zh: 不若俱死以自全。

translations.literal: Better that we all die and preserve ourselves intact.
translations.idiomatic: Better that we die together and keep ourselves whole.

sentences.zh: 」已而，攻城益急，於是劉氏與二女相繼自盡。

translations.literal: Presently the assault on the city grew more urgent; thereupon Lady Liu and her two daughters in succession took their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: The assault intensified; Lady Liu and her two daughters killed themselves one after another.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞於朝，四年五月，追封劉氏為郡君，諡曰「貞潔」，其長女諡曰「定薑」，次「肅薑」，以其事付史館。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported to court; in the fifth month of the fourth year, Lady Liu was posthumously enfeoffed as Commandery Lady, with the posthumous title "Chaste and Pure"; her elder daughter with the posthumous title "Steadfast Jiang," the younger "Solemn Jiang"; the affair was entrusted to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported the matter to court; in the fifth month of the fourth year Lady Liu was posthumously created a commandery lady with the epithet Chaste and Pure, her elder daughter Steadfast Jiang and the younger Solemn Jiang, and the case was entered in the historiographical records.

sentences.zh: 馮妙真

translations.literal: Feng Miaozhen
translations.idiomatic: Feng Miaozhen

sentences.zh: 馮妙真，刑部尚書延登之女也。

translations.literal: Feng Miaozhen was the daughter of Feng Yandeng, Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Miaozhen was a daughter of Feng Yandeng, Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 生十有八年，適進士張綎。

translations.literal: At eighteen years of age she was married to the jinshi Zhang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she married Zhang Chao, a holder of the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 興定五年，綎為洛川主簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding, Chao was chief clerk of Luochuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xingding (1221) Chao became chief clerk of Luochuan.

sentences.zh: 大元兵破葭州、綏德，遂入鄜延。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan army captured Jiazhou and Suide, and then entered Yan and Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol army took Jiazhou and Suide and swept into the Yan'an region.

sentences.zh: 鄜人震恐具守備，守臣以西路輸芻粟不時至，檄慥詣平涼督之。

translations.literal: The people of Yan were terrified and fully prepared defenses; the defending officials, because fodder and grain for the western route did not arrive in time, issued a dispatch for Chao to go to Pingliang to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yan'an were terrified and threw up defenses; because fodder for the western line failed to arrive on schedule, the defenders ordered Chao to Pingliang to hurry the supplies.

sentences.zh: 時延登為平涼行省員外郎，綎欲偕妙真以往，妙真辭曰：「舅姑老矣。

translations.literal: At that time Yandeng was an outside member of the Pingliang Branch Secretariat; Chao wished to take Miaozhen with him; Miaozhen declined, saying: "My parents-in-law are old.
translations.idiomatic: Yandeng was then an outside member of the Pingliang Branch Secretariat; Chao wanted Miaozhen to accompany him, but she refused, saying, "My parents-in-law are elderly.

sentences.zh: 雖有叔姒，妾能安乎。

translations.literal: Though there is an aunt by marriage, how can I be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Though my husband's uncle's wife is here, how could I be easy in mind?

sentences.zh: 子行，妾留奉養。

translations.literal: You go — I remain to serve them in nurture.
translations.idiomatic: You go; I will stay and care for them.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，洛川破，妙真從舅姑匿窟室，兵索得之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Luochuan fell; Miaozhen hid with her parents-in-law in a cave-room; the soldiers searched and found them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Luochuan fell; Miaozhen hid with her in-laws in a cellar until soldiers found them.

sentences.zh: 妙真泣與舅姑訣曰：「婦生不辰，不得終執箕帚，義不從辱。

translations.literal: Miaozhen wept and took leave of her parents-in-law, saying: "This wife was born at an unlucky hour and could not to the end wield broom and dustpan; in righteousness I will not submit to disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she bade her in-laws farewell: "I was born under an ill star and could not serve you to the end; I will not live to be shamed.

sentences.zh: 」即攜三子赴井死。

translations.literal: She thereupon took her three sons and went into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: She took her three sons and threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 縣人從而死者數十人。

translations.literal: Several tens of people of the county followed her in death.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen townspeople followed her into death.

sentences.zh: 明年春，綎發井得屍，殯於縣之東郭外。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year Chao opened the well and obtained the corpses, and buried them east of the outer wall of the county.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Chao opened the well, recovered the bodies, and buried them outside the eastern gate of the county seat.

sentences.zh: 死時年二十四。

translations.literal: At the time of death her age was twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-four when she died.

sentences.zh: 蒲察氏

translations.literal: Lady Pucha
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pucha

sentences.zh: 蒲察氏，字明秀，鄜州帥訥申之女，完顏長樂之妻也。

translations.literal: Of the Pucha clan, styled Mingxiu, daughter of the commander of Fuzhou Neshen, and wife of Wanyan Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pucha, courtesy name Mingxiu, was a daughter of Neshen, military commander of Fuzhou, and the wife of Wanyan Changle.

sentences.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，以長樂為總領，將兵扈從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Changle was made chief commander and was to lead troops in escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong withdrew to Guide, Changle was appointed chief commander to lead the escort force.

sentences.zh: 將行，屬蒲察氏曰：「無他言，夫人慎毋辱此身。

translations.literal: About to depart, he charged Lady Pucha, saying: "Have no other words — Madame, take care that you do not disgrace this person.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched he told Lady Pucha, "Say nothing else — only see that you do not shame yourself.

sentences.zh: 」明秀曰：「君第致身事上，無以妾為念。

translations.literal: " Mingxiu said: "My lord, simply devote your person to serving the sovereign — do not think of me as your wife.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingxiu replied, "Serve the throne with all your strength; do not give me a thought.

sentences.zh: 妾必不辱。

translations.literal: Your wife will surely not be disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: I shall not bring disgrace upon you.

sentences.zh: 」長樂一子在幼，出妻柴氏所生也，明秀撫育如己出。

translations.literal: Changle had one son still young, born of his former wife of the Chai clan; Mingxiu reared and nurtured him as if he were her own.
translations.idiomatic: Changle had one young son by his former wife of the Chai clan; Mingxiu raised him as her own.

sentences.zh: 崔立之變，驅從官妻子于省中，人自閱之。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, the wives and children of attendant officials were driven into the provincial offices for inspection, each person examining them.
translations.idiomatic: During Cui Li's coup the wives and children of court officials were herded into the provincial compound to be picked over one by one.

sentences.zh: 蒲察氏聞，以幼子付婢僕，且與之金幣，親具衣棺祭物，與家人訣曰：「崔立不道，強人妻女，兵在城下，吾何所逃，惟一死不負吾夫耳。

translations.literal: When Lady Pucha heard of it, she entrusted the young son to a maidservant together with gold and coins, personally prepared garments and coffin offerings, and took leave of her household, saying: "Cui Li is without the Way, forcibly taking men's wives and daughters; with troops below the walls, where could I flee — only death can fail to disgrace my husband.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard, she handed her little son to a maid with gold and coins, laid out her burial clothes herself, and bade her family farewell: "Cui Li is lawless, seizing men's wives and daughters; with the enemy at the walls I have nowhere to run — only death can keep me from shaming my husband.

sentences.zh: 汝等惟善養幼子。

translations.literal: You must only well nurture the young son.
translations.idiomatic: See only that you raise the boy well.

sentences.zh: 」遂自縊而死，欣然若不以死為難者。

translations.literal: She thereupon hanged herself, as if pleased and not regarding death as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Then she hanged herself, serene as though death were no hardship at all.

sentences.zh: 時年二十七。

translations.literal: Her age at that time was twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 烏古論氏

translations.literal: Lady Wugulun
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wugulun

sentences.zh: 烏古論氏，伯祥之妹，臨洮總管陀滿胡土門之妻也。

translations.literal: Of the Wugulun clan — younger sister of Boxiang, and wife of Tuoman Hutumen, military commander of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wugulun was a younger sister of Boxiang and the wife of Tuoman Hutumen, military commander of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 伯祥朝貴中聲譽藉甚，胡土門死王事。

translations.literal: Boxiang's reputation among the court nobility was very great; Hutumen died in service to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiang stood high among the court nobility; Hutumen died in the king's service.

sentences.zh: 崔立之變，衣冠家婦女多為所汙，烏古論氏謂家人曰：「吾夫不辱朝廷，我敢辱吾兄及吾夫乎。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, many wives and daughters of official families were defiled; Lady Wugulun said to her household: "My husband did not disgrace the court — how dare I disgrace my elder brother and my husband!
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Li's coup came, many gentry women were violated; Lady Wugulun told her household, "My husband did not shame the throne — how could I shame my brother and my husband!

sentences.zh: 」即自縊。

translations.literal: " She thereupon hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She hanged herself at once.

sentences.zh: 一婢從死。

translations.literal: One maidservant followed her in death.
translations.idiomatic: One maid died with her.

sentences.zh: 素蘭妻

translations.literal: Wife of Su Lan
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Su Lan

sentences.zh: 參政完顏素蘭妻，亡其姓氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Grand Councilor Wanyan Su Lan — her surname is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Grand Councilor Wanyan Su Lan — her family name is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 當崔立之變，謂所親曰：「吾夫有天下重名，吾豈肯隨眾陷身以辱吾夫乎。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, she said to those close to her: "My husband bears a weighty name throughout the realm — how could I follow the crowd and plunge my person into disgrace to shame my husband!
translations.idiomatic: During Cui Li's upheaval she told her intimates, "My husband's name weighs on the empire — how could I sink with the mob and shame him!

sentences.zh: 今日一死固當，但不可無名而死，亦不可離吾家而死。

translations.literal: To die today is surely fitting — yet one must not die without a name, nor die outside one's own house.
translations.idiomatic: Death today is only right — but one must not die nameless, nor die outside one's own roof.

sentences.zh: 」即自縊於室。

translations.literal: She thereupon hanged herself in her chamber.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself in her own room.

sentences.zh: 忙哥妻

translations.literal: Wife of Mang Ge
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Mang Ge

sentences.zh: 溫特罕氏，夫完顏忙哥，五朵山宣差提控回裏不之子也，系出蕭王。

translations.literal: Of the Wentehan clan — husband Wanyan Mang Ge, son of the Xuan-chai Tikuilibu of Wuduoshan, of descent from Prince Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Wentehan clan — wife of Wanyan Mang Ge, son of the frontier commissioner Tikuilibu of Wuduoshan and a descendant of Prince Xiao.

sentences.zh: 忙哥叔父益都，節度秦州，為大元兵所攻，適病不能軍，忙哥為提控，獨當一面。

translations.literal: Mang Ge's uncle Yidu was military commissioner of Qinzhou; he was attacked by the Great Yuan army; just then he fell ill and could not command the army; Mang Ge was Tikuil and alone bore one flank.
translations.idiomatic: Mang Ge's uncle Yidu held Qinzhou when the Mongols attacked; Yidu fell ill and could not take the field, and Mang Ge as frontier commissioner held one sector alone.

sentences.zh: 兵退而益都死，忙哥以城守功世襲謀克，收充奉禦。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew Yidu died; Mang Ge by merit of defending the city inherited the post of military commander and was enrolled as an attendant of the inner service.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew Yidu died; Mang Ge inherited a company commandership for holding the city and entered service as an inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 及崔立之變，忙哥義不受辱，與其妻訣。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, Mang Ge in righteousness would not accept disgrace and took leave of his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Li's coup broke out, Mang Ge, holding that he could not live in dishonor, bade his wife farewell.

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「君能為國家死，我不能為君死乎。

translations.literal: His wife said: "You can die for the state — can I not die for you?
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "You can die for the dynasty — cannot I die for you?

sentences.zh: 」一婢曰：「主死，婢將安歸。

translations.literal: A maid said: "If the master dies, whither shall the maid return?
translations.idiomatic: A maid said, "If my master dies, where shall I go?

sentences.zh: 」是日，夫婦以一繩同縊，婢從之。

translations.literal: On that day husband and wife hanged themselves on one cord; the maid followed them.
translations.idiomatic: That day husband and wife shared one rope; the maid followed.

sentences.zh: 尹氏，完顏豬兒之妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Yin — wife of Wanyan Zhuer,
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin was the wife of Wanyan Zhuer,

sentences.zh: 豬兒系出蕭王，天興二年正月從哀宗為南面元帥，戰死黃陵岡。

translations.literal: Zhuer of descent from Prince Xiao; in the first month of the second year of Tianxing he followed Emperor Aizong as southern-route commander-in-chief and died in battle at Huangling Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: a descendant of Prince Xiao; in the first month of the second year of Tianxing (1233) he followed Emperor Aizong as southern-route commander and was killed at Huangling Ridge.

sentences.zh: 其妻金源郡夫人聞豬兒死，聚家資焚之，遂自縊，年三十一。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady of Jinyuan Commandery, upon hearing of Zhuer's death gathered the household valuables and burned them, and thereupon hanged herself — her age thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady of Jinyuan Commandery heard of his death she burned the family wealth and hanged herself at thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 豬兒贈官，弟長住即日詔補護衛。

translations.literal: Zhuer was granted posthumous office; his younger brother Changzhu was that very day ordered by edict to be enrolled as a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuer received posthumous honors; his younger brother Changzhu was the same day enrolled in the guard by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 聶孝女

translations.literal: Nie Xiaonu
translations.idiomatic: Nie Xiaonu

sentences.zh: 聶孝女，字舜英，尚書左右司員外郎天驥之長女也。

translations.literal: Nie Xiaonu, styled Shunying, was the eldest daughter of Nie Tianji, outside member of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Xiaonu, courtesy name Shunying, was the eldest daughter of Nie Tianji, an outside member of the Left and Right Secretariat bureaus.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，適進士張伯豪。

translations.literal: At twenty-three she was married to the jinshi Zhang Bohao.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three she married Zhang Bohao, a jinshi degree holder.

sentences.zh: 伯豪卒，歸父母家。

translations.literal: When Bohao died she returned to her parents' home.
translations.idiomatic: When Bohao died she returned to her father's house.

sentences.zh: 及哀宗遷歸德，天驥留汴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong withdrew to Guide, Tianji stayed behind at Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 崔立劫殺宰相，天驥被創甚，日夜悲泣，恨不即死。

translations.literal: At Cui Li's seizure and killing of the grand councilors, Tianji was severely wounded; day and night he grieved and wept, resenting that he could not die at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Li seized and murdered the grand councilors, Tianji was badly wounded; day and night he wept, bitter that he could not die at once.

sentences.zh: 舜英謁醫救療百方，至刲其股雜他肉以進，而天驥竟死。

translations.literal: Shunying sought physicians and applied a hundred remedies for healing; she even cut flesh from her thigh, mixed it with other meat, and presented it — yet Tianji ultimately died.
translations.idiomatic: Shunying summoned doctors and tried every cure; she even cut flesh from her thigh, mixed it with other meat, and fed it to him — yet Tianji died all the same.

sentences.zh: 時京城圍久食盡，閭巷間有嫁妻易一飽者，重以崔立之變，剽奪暴淩，無複人理。

translations.literal: At that time the capital had long been besieged and food was exhausted; among lanes and alleys there were those who sold wives to trade for a full meal; added to Cui Li's upheaval, plundering and violent abuse — there was no longer any human reason.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had been besieged so long that food was gone; in the alleys men sold their wives for a single meal; on top of Cui Li's coup came looting and outrage until human decency vanished.

sentences.zh: 舜英頗讀書知義理，自以年尚少艾，夫既亡，父又死非命，比為兵所汙，何若從吾父于地下乎。

translations.literal: Shunying had read books and knew righteousness; she herself thought: her years were still few and fair, her husband already dead, her father dead not by natural causes — if she were defiled by soldiers, how better to follow her father in the underworld?
translations.idiomatic: Shunying had read and understood moral principle; she reasoned that she was still young and comely, her husband gone, her father slain unnaturally — if soldiers violated her, was it not better to join her father underground?

sentences.zh: 葬其父之明日，絕脰而死。

translations.literal: On the day after burying her father she broke her neck and died.
translations.idiomatic: The day after her father's burial she broke her own neck and died.

sentences.zh: 一時士女賢之，有為泣下者。

translations.literal: Men and women of the time honored her; some wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised her; some wept at her death.

sentences.zh: 其家以舜英合葬張伯豪之墓。

translations.literal: Her household buried Shunying together with Zhang Bohao's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Her family buried her beside Zhang Bohao's grave.

sentences.zh: 仲德妻

translations.literal: Wife of Zhong De
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Zhong De

sentences.zh: 完顏仲德妻，不知其族氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Wanyan Zhong De — her clan is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Zhong De's wife — her clan is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 崔立之變，妻自毀其容服，攜妾及二子紿以采蔬，自汴走蔡。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, the wife destroyed her fine appearance and garments, took a concubine and two sons, pretended to be gathering vegetables, and fled from Bian to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: During Cui Li's coup she disfigured her face and ruined her fine clothes, took a concubine and two sons, pretended to go out gathering greens, and fled from Bianliang to Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蔡被圍，丁男皆乘城拒守，謂仲德曰：「事勢若此，丈夫能為國出力，婦人獨不能耶！

translations.literal: When Cai was besieged, all able-bodied men mounted the walls to resist; she said to Zhong De: "The situation being thus, a great man can exert himself for the state — cannot a woman alone do so!
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was besieged and every able man manned the walls, she told Zhong De, "Matters stand so — a man can give his strength for the state; cannot a woman do the same!

sentences.zh: 」率諸命婦自作一軍，親運矢石於城下，城中婦女爭出繼之。

translations.literal: " She led the titled ladies to form an army of their own, personally transporting arrows and stones below the wall; the women of the city vied to go out and follow her.
translations.idiomatic: " She rallied the noble wives into a corps of their own and herself hauled arrows and stones at the foot of the wall; women throughout the city rushed out to join her.

sentences.zh: 城破自盡。

translations.literal: When the city fell she took her own life.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she killed herself.

sentences.zh: 寶符李氏

translations.literal: Lady Li of Baofu
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of Baofu

sentences.zh: 哀宗寶符李氏，國亡從後妃北遷，至宣德州，居摩訶院，日夕寢處佛殿中，作幡旆。

translations.literal: Lady Li of Baofu of Emperor Aizong — when the state perished she followed the consorts north; reaching Xuande Prefecture, she dwelt at the Mahā monastery, day and night sleeping within the Buddha hall, making banners and pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of Baofu, a consort of Emperor Aizong, followed the imperial women north when the dynasty fell; at Xuande Prefecture she lived in the Mahā monastery, sleeping in the Buddha hall by day and night and sewing banners.

sentences.zh: 會當赴龍庭，將發，即於佛像前自縊死，且自書門紙曰：「寶符禦侍此處身故。

translations.literal: When the time came to go to the Dragon Court and they were about to depart, she hanged herself before the Buddha image and moreover wrote on the door paper: "Baofu the imperial attendant died here.
translations.idiomatic: When they were to set out for the northern court she hanged herself before the Buddha image and wrote on the door, "Baofu the imperial attendant died here.

sentences.zh: 」後人至其處，見其遺跡，憐而哀之。

translations.literal: " Later people coming to the place, seeing her traces, pitied and mourned her.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came afterward, finding what she left, pitied and mourned her.

sentences.zh: 張鳳奴

translations.literal: Zhang Fengnu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fengnu

sentences.zh: 天興元年，北兵攻城，矢石之際忽見一女子呼於城下曰：「我倡女張鳳奴也，許州破被俘至此。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxing, the northern army besieged the city; amid arrows and stones a woman suddenly called from below the wall: "I am the singing-girl Zhang Fengnu; when Xuzhou fell I was captured and brought here.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing (1232) the northern army besieged the city; amid flying arrows and stones a woman suddenly cried from below the wall, "I am the courtesan Zhang Fengnu; when Xuzhou fell I was taken captive and brought here.

sentences.zh: 彼軍不日去矣，諸君努力為國堅守，無為所欺也。

translations.literal: Their army will before long depart — all of you, strive to hold firm for the state, and do not be deceived!
translations.idiomatic: Their army will leave before long — hold fast for the dynasty and do not be fooled!

sentences.zh: 」言竟，投濠而死。

translations.literal: When she had finished speaking she cast herself into the moat and died.
translations.idiomatic: She finished speaking and threw herself into the moat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使馳祭於西門。

translations.literal: The court dispatched an envoy to perform sacrifices at the west gate with all speed.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent an envoy at once to sacrifice at the west gate.

sentences.zh: 正大、天興之際，婦人節義可知者特數人耳。

translations.literal: In the Zhengda and Tianxing periods, the integrity of women that can be known numbers only a few persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengda and Tianxing eras only a handful of women whose fidelity can be known appear in the record.

sentences.zh: 鳳奴之事別史錄之。

translations.literal: Fengnu's affair is recorded in another history.
translations.idiomatic: Fengnu's story is entered elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 蓋亦有所激雲。

translations.literal: Perhaps there was also something that stirred them, it may be said.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps each was moved by something beyond herself — so one may say.
